one_liner: x64-tuned C++17 big-integer library with GMP-style mpn kernels, Toom-Cook and FFT multiplication; has a GMP harness but publishes no numbers.
what_it_does: WJR is a single-maintainer C++17 utility library whose wjr::biginteger module provides an mpz-like class (basic_biginteger with heap, fixed, in-place and stack-allocator storage variants) plus low-level limb functions named after GMP's mpn layer (addc_n, subc_1, mul_1, addmul_1, submul_1, div_qr_1, div_qr_2, mul, sqr). The class API mirrors GMP's mpz names: addmul, submul, tdiv/fdiv/cdiv quotient and remainder, mul_2exp, pow, powmod, urandom, from_chars and to_chars. It is not a drop-in for GMP's C API; the same repository also ships JSON, string and ring-buffer modules, linked via CMake targets such as wjr::biginteger.
how_it_is_fast: Small and medium sizes use hand-tuned x64 kernels (optional NASM assembly modules, intrinsics guarded by WJR_HAS_* macros) for carry-propagating add/sub and multiply-accumulate. Larger products switch through Toom-2 to Toom-5 thresholds (toom22 to toom55, plus unbalanced toom32/42/43/53/63) and then to a Schönhage-Strassen FFT with mulmod_bnm1 and mulmod_bknp1 wrapping, whose sources keep GMP's mpn_mul_fft structure, comments and macro names through a gmp-helper.hpp shim. Temporary limbs come from a stack allocator (unique_stack_allocator) instead of malloc.
when_to_use: You want a GMP-style integer class in C++17 on x86-64 without linking libgmp, and are willing to benchmark it yourself first.
Operand sizes of a few to roughly a thousand 64-bit limbs, which is the range the repository's own benchmark sweeps (4 to 256 limbs for most kernels, up to 1024 for mul_n and sqr).
Code that already uses WJR's JSON or string modules, where the big-integer type comes for free.
Studying a modern C++ restructuring of GMP's mpn algorithms (Toom, FFT, division, radix conversion).
when_not_to_use: You need evidence: there are no published results against GMP anywhere in the README, docs, issues or CI summaries; the CI benchmark only compares to its own previous run.
Non-x64 targets or AMD-specific tuning: the README says most optimizations are x64-only and AMD has not been tested or tuned.
Code that relies on exceptions: the README says exception handling is poorly supported.
Shared-library builds: the README TODO list says unique_stack_allocator under a dynamic library still needs fixing.
You need gcd, integer square root, rationals or floats: none of these appear in the biginteger header (GMP, FLINT or Boost.Multiprecision cover them).

integration.dependencies: fmt (git submodule in third-party/); optional NASM for x64 assembly; GMP only for the comparison benchmarks and tests
integration.min_toolchain: C++17, 64-bit, CMake; CI tests Clang 17-20, GCC 9 and 11-14 on Linux and MSVC/Clang on Windows
integration.platforms: x86-64 Linux and Windows (main optimizations); other 64-bit targets via generic fallbacks
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the class method names mirror mpz (addmul, tdiv_qr, powmod, ...) but it is a C++ class, not the mpz_t/mpn C API

gotchas: The top-level CMakeLists.txt adds -march=native for every GCC/Clang build, so binaries built this way are tied to the build machine's CPU.
C++20 is disabled by default (WJR_DISABLE_CXX_20=ON); -DWJR_DISABLE_EXCEPTIONS=ON compiles with -fno-exceptions.

License provenance: the FFT and mulmod files (src/biginteger/detail/fft.cpp, mulmod_bknp1.cpp) carry GMP's comments and macros but only a 2025 wjr copyright header, while the repository is LGPL-2.1; GMP itself is LGPLv3+/GPLv2+, so check provenance before redistributing.
To get GMP numbers you must configure with -DWJR_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=ON, -DWJR_BENCHMARK_PROFILE=all and libgmp installed; the CI 'all' profile runs 1 repetition at 0.03 s minimum time.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick wjr over Boost.Multiprecision cpp_int or libzahl only if you need GMP-scale algorithms (Toom-Cook, FFT) in a C++ class without libgmp and can verify speed yourself; mp++ or FLINT are the safer choices when linking GMP is acceptable and you want measured, maintained speedups.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing was measured publicly: benchmarks/src/biginteger.cpp pairs wjr_* and gmp_* Google Benchmark cases (mpn_add_n, mpn_mul, mpn_tdiv_qr, mpn_get_str and others) at 4 to 1024 limbs, built Release with -march=native, but no result files, tables or CPU models are published and the weekly CI on ubuntu-24.04 runners builds without GMP by default.
status_note: Actively developed (last commit 2026-08-27, 1,150 commits) by one maintainer with 7 stars and no issues filed; LGPL-2.1, so it is usable via dynamic or relinkable linking, but treat it as unproven.
